faq.question: Where do you start with an HSSE approach?
faq.answer: Everything starts with an initial assessment: we review your existing practices, regulatory obligations and priority risks. On that basis, we build a step-by-step roadmap together, tailored to your resources and timeline.

faq.question: Is ISO 45001 certification essential?
faq.answer: No, certification is not always necessary. Many companies improve safety performance without pursuing certification. We help you decide based on your clients' requirements, your sector and your ambitions; if certification makes sense, we support you all the way to the audit.

faq.question: How long does an engagement last?
faq.answer: A typical engagement runs from 3 to 12 months depending on the size of the organization and its starting point. Regular milestones allow us to adjust the plan and measure progress with concrete indicators.

cases.title: Construction company – full structuring
cases.context: A public works company with no formal prevention system, facing recurring site shutdowns after incidents.
cases.result: An operational HSSE committee was set up, two internal coordinators were trained, and reported accidents were cut by more than half within one year.

cases.title: Public institution – audit preparation
cases.context: An institution seeking to align its practices with ISO 45001 to meet donor requirements.
cases.result: Complete gap analysis, management system documentation and team support through to management review.

faq.question: Is the risk assessment document mandatory for all companies?
faq.answer: Yes, every employer must document their occupational risk assessment, regardless of headcount. The single document must be updated at least annually and whenever working conditions change significantly.

faq.question: How is a risk assessment carried out?
faq.answer: We combine field observations, interviews with teams and analysis of existing data (incidents, absenteeism). Each risk is then rated by severity and likelihood, which allows prevention actions to be prioritized.

faq.question: What deliverable do we receive?
faq.answer: You receive the complete single risk document, a risk map by position or workshop, and a prioritized action plan with concrete, realistic measures to implement.

cases.title: Production workshop – risk mapping
cases.context: A small industrial site with no clear view of its risks and several unanalyzed minor accidents.
cases.result: Risk document completed in 4 weeks, 23 risks identified and rated, prioritized prevention plan validated by management and teams.

cases.title: Distribution network – regulatory update
cases.context: A multi-site SME whose risk document was outdated and inconsistent from one site to another.
cases.result: A common methodology deployed across all sites, harmonized documents and an annual updating process established in-house.

faq.question: What is the difference between a procedure and an emergency plan?
faq.answer: The procedure describes how to work safely day to day; the emergency plan organizes the collective response to a serious event (fire, leak, injury). They complement each other: one prevents, the other limits the consequences.

faq.question: Should teams practice regularly?
faq.answer: Yes, it is essential. An untested plan remains theoretical. We recommend at least one drill per year per major scenario, with a debriefing and document update after each exercise.

faq.question: Do you tailor documents to our activity?
faq.answer: Always. No generic procedure works: we write based on your actual facilities, equipment and operating methods, involving the people who perform the work.

cases.title: Storage facility – fire plan
cases.context: A warehouse of flammable materials with no structured guidelines or proven evacuation organization.
cases.result: A complete emergency plan was written, a response team designated and trained, and the first full-scale drill successfully completed within the quarter.

cases.title: Private clinic – hygiene procedures
cases.context: A healthcare facility needing to formalize its protocols for an accreditation process.
cases.result: A series of operational procedures validated by staff, with signage and awareness materials deployed across all departments.

faq.question: Where should you start to reduce your environmental footprint?
faq.answer: With an impact assessment: energy consumption, water, waste, emissions. This initial snapshot identifies the most significant areas and focuses effort where the gain is greatest.

faq.question: Do you handle environmental regulatory compliance?
faq.answer: Yes. We carry out compliance audits, identify the obligations applicable to your activity and build a progressive, documented compliance schedule.

faq.question: Do you work with local authorities?
faq.answer: We know the Central African institutional framework well and support our clients in technical exchanges with the administration when it helps their case.

cases.title: Agribusiness – waste management
cases.context: A processing unit accumulating organic and plastic waste with no treatment channel.
cases.result: A sorting and recovery scheme was set up, contracts established with local channels, and landfill volumes significantly reduced from the first year.

cases.title: Infrastructure project – impact study
cases.context: A project developer needing to produce an environmental and social impact assessment for financing.
cases.result: Study conducted according to the standards expected by donors; the environmental and social management plan annexed to the file was accepted.

faq.question: At what stage should you reach out to us?
faq.answer: At any stage: validating an idea, structuring a young business, or organizing an existing structure that wants to move up a level. The starting point is always a shared diagnosis of your situation.

faq.question: Is the Business Model Canvas suitable for local SMEs?
faq.answer: It is precisely a valuable tool for them: it shows the whole business on one page, highlights fragile assumptions and allows quick adjustments without committing major resources.

faq.question: Do you help prepare bank-ready business plans?
faq.answer: Yes, we develop complete, credible business plans: economic model, three-year financial forecast and pitch, presented in the format expected by banks and investors.

cases.title: Food startup – scaling up
cases.context: A profitable family business organized informally, held back in its growth by the lack of structure.
cases.result: Business Model Canvas clarified, key roles defined, a three-year business plan produced and bank financing unlocked.

cases.title: Retail shop – margin recovery
cases.context: A multi-product store whose profitability was eroding without identifiable causes.
cases.result: Margin analysis by product family, revised pricing policy and simple monthly monitoring set up with the manager.

faq.question: What is the typical duration of a coaching engagement?
faq.answer: Coaching cycles generally run from 6 to 12 months, with regular sessions (monthly or bi-monthly) and measurable intermediate goals. The pace adapts to your availability and current priorities.

faq.question: Does post-training follow-up cover all our trained staff?
faq.answer: Yes, we offer post-training follow-up to anchor learning: feedback sessions, resolving difficulties encountered in the field and adjusting practices. That is what turns training into lasting skill.

faq.question: Do you work with very small businesses?
faq.answer: Absolutely. Our packages are modular and designed for micro-business and solo entrepreneur budgets: we start with the essentials, then expand at the pace of your progress.

cases.title: Solo entrepreneur – structured launch
cases.context: A project owner with strong know-how but no experience running a business.
cases.result: Six months of coaching: offer clarified, prices positioned, first clients signed and simple management tools adopted daily.

cases.title: Service SME – handing over responsibility
cases.context: A business owner wanting to delegate day-to-day management to focus on commercial development.
cases.result: Organization redesigned, an internal supervisor coached for one year and operational responsibilities effectively transferred.

faq.title: Got any
faq.description: Find answers to the most common questions about our services, training programs and how we work.

items.question: Which areas do you cover?
items.answer: We primarily operate in Bangui and the Central African Republic. Depending on the mission, we can travel to other cities in the country and across the region.

items.question: Can training be held at our premises?
items.answer: Yes, most of our training programs can be delivered directly at your facilities. This is even recommended for hands-on training that requires on-site practice.

items.question: How long does a typical HSSE consulting engagement last?
items.answer: It depends on the project's complexity. An audit may take 2 to 5 days, while ISO 45001 compliance typically spans 3 to 6 months with regular follow-ups.

items.question: How does an occupational risk assessment work?
items.answer: We conduct a thorough assessment: team interviews, on-site inspections, and document analysis. We then deliver a detailed report with the DUERP and a prioritized action plan.

items.question: Do you offer certified training?
items.answer: Our training programs issue competence certificates recognized by industry professionals. We can also prepare your teams for ISO 45001 certification.

items.question: How do I request a quote?
items.answer: Use the contact form or email us directly at contact.cmc@gmail.com describing your needs. We will get back to you within 48 hours with a tailored proposal.
